messages.author: 4076f5688b45a1a5
messages.subject: Problem with temporal dimensionality
parts:
Good morning!
I have a problem with the model I'm working on: the data structure is based on 49 relevation of pollutant in an italian region, repeated 364 days. 
I'm fitting an spde + ar(1) model for the spatio temporal residual using inlabru. The problem is that it works very well with 50 days, but it crushes (same code, same data, but extendend) when I try to use more days (already with 90 days it crushes) and the error is the following: 

parse section=[10] name=[INLA.pardiso] type=[PARDISO]
    inla_parse_pardiso...
        section[INLA.pardiso]
        verbose[0]
        debug[0]
        parallel.reordering[1]
        nrhs[-1]
    parse section=[9Error in inla.inlaprogram.has.crashed() :
  The inla-program exited with an error. Unless you interupted it yourself, please rerun with verbose=TRUE and check the output carefully.
  If this does not help, please contact the developers at <he...@r-inla.org>.
Warning in iinla(model = info[["model"]], lhoods = info[["lhoods"]], options = info[["options"]]) :
  iinla: Problem in inla: Error in inla.core.safe(formula = formula, family = family, contrasts = contrasts,  :
  *** Fail to get good enough initial values. Maybe it is due to something else.
iinla: Problem in inla: 1: bru(cmp, lik, options = list(verbose = TRUE, inla.mode = "experimental"))
2: iinla(model = info[["model"]], lhoods = info[["lhoods"]], options = info[[ [...]
3: try_callstack(...)
4: do.call(INLA::inla, inla.options.merged, envir = environment(model$effects))
5: (function (formula = NULL, family = "gaussian", contrasts = NULL,
       data = NULL, quantiles = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), E = NULL,
       offset = NULL, scale = NULL, weights = NULL, Ntrials = NULL,
       strata = NULL, lp.scale = NULL, link.covariates = NULL, verbose = FALSE,
       lincomb = NULL, selection = NULL, control.compute = list(),
       control.predictor = list(), control.family = list(), control.inla = list(),
       control.fixed = list(), control.mode = list(), control.expert = list(),
     [... truncated]
iinla: Giving up and returning last successfully obtained result for diagnostic purposes.

Moreover, I'd like to ask if there's a way to speed up somehow computation, maybe with some tricky options. Right now the call is the following:

#model components
cmp = logPM10 ~ Intercept(1) +
  SPDE(coordinates, model = spde,
       group = time,  control.group = list(model = "ar1")) + Quota

lik <- like(formula = logPM10 ~ Intercept + SPDE + Quota,
            family = "gaussian",
            data = emilia.18.q)

#started at 18/10/2022 19:48

fit = bru(cmp, lik,
          options = list(
            verbose = TRUE,
            inla.mode = "experimental"
          ))

Thank you very much! 
Alessandro

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problem with temporal dimensionality
parts:
What's the size of the latent component ( spde$n.spde x 90)? Perhaps
you're running out of memory?
I don't see the 49 different pollutants appearing here; are you
running separate models? Then that shouldn't be relevant to the
problem.

For greater speed (given enough memory) but only results at the
posterior mode for the hyperparameters, use option
control.inla=list(int.strategy="eb").

Finn
